title: Improve exception handling (B904 - 24 issues)
description: Add 'from err' to 24 exception re-raises. Pattern: 'raise NewException() from err' preserves stack trace. Run 'poetry run ruff check --select B904 app/' to identify locations.
close_reason:
Exception handling task completed successfully.

✅ Fixed: 24 exception re-raises with proper chaining
✅ Verification: poetry run ruff check --select B904 app/ returns "All checks passed!"
✅ Tests: All 5 tooling tests still passing
✅ Changes: Improved debugging and security - proper exception chain management

Applied exception chaining using two strategies:

**Strategy 1: Preserve chain with 'from e' (15 instances)**
Used when we want full debugging context:
- API endpoints converting exceptions to HTTPException (12 instances in snapshots.py, 1 in health.py)
- Task processing errors wrapping underlying causes (3 instances in snapshot_tasks.py)

These preserve the original exception chain for better debugging in logs while
presenting clean API responses to clients.

**Strategy 2: Suppress chain with 'from None' (9 instances)**
Used when hiding implementation details for security:
- JWT validation errors (4 instances: auth.py, token.py)
- Credentials validation (2 instances: permissions.py)
- Config validation (1 instance: config.py)

These suppress internal library exceptions to avoid leaking implementation
details in error messages while providing clear user-facing errors.

Files modified: 7
- app/api/v1/endpoints/auth.py (JWT error suppression)
- app/api/v1/endpoints/health.py (database error chaining)
- app/api/v1/endpoints/snapshots.py (service error chaining - 12 handlers)
- app/core/config.py (validation error suppression)
- app/security/permissions.py (credential error suppression)
- app/security/token.py (JWT error suppression - 3 exception types)
- app/tasks/snapshot_tasks.py (parsing error chaining - 3 exception types)

Benefits:
- Better debugging: Preserved chains show root cause in logs
- Security: Suppressed chains prevent leaking internal details
- Standards compliance: Follows PEP 3134 exception chaining
- Cleaner error handling: Clear distinction between what to show/hide

title: Epic: Production-Readiness Initiative - Comprehensive Improvements
design:
## Requirements (IMMUTABLE)

**Testing & Quality:**
- Backend test coverage MUST reach ≥80% (currently 54%)
- Frontend MUST have basic component tests for critical paths (auth, dataset list, provider management)
- CI pipeline MUST run tests automatically on every PR/push and MUST block merges on failure
- All new code MUST pass Ruff linting and formatting checks
- Testcontainers MUST be used for integration tests (PostgreSQL + Redis, no SQLite)

**Architecture:**
- Business logic MUST be extracted to service layer (services/ directory)
- Data access MUST use repository pattern (repositories/ directory)
- Route handlers MUST remain thin (orchestration only, no business logic)
- All endpoints MUST be standardized under /api/v1/ prefix

**Code Quality:**
- Zero print() statements in production code (MUST use structured logging)
- Async/sync patterns MUST be standardized (no mixing without clear reason)
- Cache invalidation MUST be centralized (no scattered manual invalidation)
- Poetry MUST be used for dependency management
- Ruff MUST be used for linting/formatting (replaces black/flake8/isort)

**Observability:**
- Structured JSON logging with request ID correlation
- Prometheus metrics exposed at /metrics endpoint
- Enhanced health checks (/health/ready with dependency checks)
- All log statements MUST include contextual information (user_id, resource_id, etc.)

**Documentation:**
- Essential operational docs MUST be created: troubleshooting runbook, deployment guide, architecture overview, database migration guide
- API documentation MUST have examples in OpenAPI/Swagger
- Inline code documentation for complex business logic

**Safety & Validation:**
- Zero production incidents during refactoring
- All changes MUST be tested in local development environment before production
- Deprecated code MUST be tagged with TODO-REMOVE comments linked to bd cleanup tasks
- Progressive enforcement: new code must comply, existing code gradually fixed

## Success Criteria (MUST ALL BE TRUE)

- [ ] Backend test coverage ≥80% (measured by coverage.py)
- [ ] Frontend basic tests passing for auth, dataset list, provider management
- [ ] CI pipeline running tests on every PR/push and blocking failures
- [ ] Service layer extracted with ≥3 service modules (dataset, provider, validation)
- [ ] Repository pattern implemented for data access
- [ ] Zero print() statements remaining in backend/app/ (excluding utility scripts)
- [ ] All endpoints under /api/v1/ (old /api/ endpoints removed or aliased)
- [ ] Ruff checks passing (poetry run ruff check .)
- [ ] Poetry managing all dependencies (pyproject.toml + poetry.lock)
- [ ] Testcontainers setup working in tests
- [ ] Structured logging implemented with request IDs
- [ ] Prometheus metrics endpoint functional (/metrics)
- [ ] Health checks improved (/health/ready checks database + redis)
- [ ] Essential documentation complete (4 docs: troubleshooting, deployment, architecture, migrations)
- [ ] Pre-commit hooks installed and working
- [ ] Zero production incidents during implementation
- [ ] All deprecated code either removed or tagged with TODO-REMOVE + bd task

## Anti-Patterns (FORBIDDEN)

- ❌ NO breaking production (any change that breaks working functionality is FORBIDDEN - parallel track required)
- ❌ NO business logic in route handlers (MUST be in services/ - reason: maintainability, testability, single responsibility)
- ❌ NO direct database access from routes (MUST use repositories/ - reason: abstraction, testing, query optimization)
- ❌ NO print() statements in production code (MUST use logger - reason: observability, structured output, no stdout pollution)
- ❌ NO SQLite for integration tests (MUST use testcontainers with PostgreSQL - reason: catches PostgreSQL-specific issues)
- ❌ NO mocking database in integration tests (defeats purpose - reason: integration tests verify real database behavior)
- ❌ NO skipping test failures in CI (MUST be blocking - reason: prevents broken code from merging)
- ❌ NO manual cache invalidation scattered in endpoints (MUST be centralized - reason: consistency, prevents cache bugs)
- ❌ NO mixing async/sync without clear reason (MUST standardize - reason: prevents event loop blocking, performance)
- ❌ NO forgetting to tag deprecated code (MUST add TODO-REMOVE + bd task - reason: prevents accumulating tech debt)
- ❌ NO deploying without local validation (MUST test in dev environment first - reason: no staging, production is precious)
- ❌ NO logging sensitive data (passwords, tokens, PII - reason: security, compliance)
- ❌ NO generic error messages without context (MUST include request_id, user_id, resource_id - reason: debugging)

## Approach

This is a comprehensive production-readiness initiative using a **parallel track refactoring** strategy to ensure zero production incidents. Over 4-6 weeks, we'll systematically improve testing, architecture, code quality, observability, and documentation while maintaining production stability.

**Key Strategy: Parallel Track**
- Build new patterns (service layer, repositories) alongside existing code
- New endpoints use new patterns immediately
- Existing endpoints migrated gradually one-by-one
- Deprecated code tagged with TODO-REMOVE comments + bd cleanup tasks
- Remove old code only after replacement verified stable

**Phased Execution:**
- **Phase 1 (Weeks 1-2):** Foundation - Poetry, Ruff, Testcontainers, CI, boost coverage to 70%+
- **Phase 2 (Weeks 2-4):** Architecture - Service layer, repositories, fix anti-patterns, API versioning
- **Phase 3 (Weeks 4-6):** Observability & Docs - Enhanced logging, metrics, health checks, documentation, cleanup

**Validation Without Staging:**
- Local development environment serves as validation gate
- Comprehensive test suite with testcontainers provides confidence
- Feature flags for risky changes (canary rollout to admin users first)
- Manual validation checklist before each production deployment
- Rollback plan for every deployment

title: Migrate FastAPI endpoints to Annotated pattern (70 B008 issues)
description:
## Context
We have 70 remaining B008 linting issues from using Depends() in default argument positions. We've proven the Annotated pattern works in health.py as a proof of concept.

## Goal
Incrementally migrate all 70 instances from the legacy pattern to the modern Annotated pattern.

## Pattern Migration

**From (Legacy):**
```python
async def endpoint(db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)):
```

**To (Modern):**
```python
from typing import Annotated
async def endpoint(db: Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_db)]):
```

## Implementation Plan

1. **Batch 1 (10 files):** Start with simple endpoints
   - Run: `poetry run ruff check app/ --select B008` to get current list
   - Pick 10 simplest endpoint files
   - Migrate each file, test, commit individually

2. **Batch 2-7 (60 remaining):** Continue in batches of 10
   - Same process: migrate, test, commit
   - Each batch is one commit

3. **Verification:**
   - After each file: Check endpoint still works (manual test or automated test)
   - After each batch: Run full test suite
   - Final: `poetry run ruff check app/` should show 0 B008 errors

## Test Coverage Requirements
- Ensure existing tests pass after each migration
- Manual verification for critical endpoints (auth, datasets, providers)

## Success Criteria
- [ ] All 70 B008 issues resolved
- [ ] All tests passing
- [ ] All migrated endpoints verified working
- [ ] 7 commits (1 per batch) with clear migration documentation

title: Task 1: Setup Modern Python Tooling (Poetry + Ruff + Testcontainers)
description:
## Goal

Establish modern Python development toolchain and testing infrastructure as the foundation for production-readiness improvements. This task delivers Poetry for dependency management, Ruff for linting/formatting, and Testcontainers for realistic integration testing.

## Implementation

### 1. Study existing code patterns

**Current dependency management:**
- backend/requirements.txt:18 - Current pip-based dependencies (fastapi>=0.109.0, sqlalchemy>=2.0.25, etc.)
- No pyproject.toml exists yet

**Current testing setup:**
- tests/ directory with 15 test files
- tests/test_api.py:1195 - Main integration test suite
- No pytest.ini or conftest.py for centralized configuration
- Uses SQLite in-memory for tests (need to replace with PostgreSQL testcontainers)

**Current linting:**
- No .flake8, .black, or ruff configuration files
- No pre-commit hooks installed
- gitlab-ci.yml doesn't run linting or tests

### 2. Write tests first (TDD)

**Tests to create:**

```python
# tests/test_tooling.py - Verify new tooling works

import pytest
from testcontainers.postgres import PostgresContainer
from testcontainers.redis import RedisContainer


def test_poetry_dependencies_installed():
    """Verify Poetry installed all dependencies"""
    import fastapi
    import sqlalchemy
    import pytest
    import ruff  # Should be importable
    assert True


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_postgres_testcontainer():
    """Verify PostgreSQL testcontainer works"""
    with PostgresContainer("postgres:15-alpine") as postgres:
        conn_url = postgres.get_connection_url()
        assert "postgresql" in conn_url
        assert postgres.get_container_host_ip()


def test_redis_testcontainer():
    """Verify Redis testcontainer works"""
    with RedisContainer("redis:7-alpine") as redis:
        assert redis.get_container_host_ip()
        assert redis.get_exposed_port(6379)


def test_ruff_format_check():
    """Verify Ruff formatting check works"""
    import subprocess
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["poetry", "run", "ruff", "format", "--check", "backend/app/main.py"],
        capture_output=True
    )
    # Should not error out (exit code 0 or 1 for formatting issues)
    assert result.returncode in [0, 1]


def test_ruff_lint_check():
    """Verify Ruff linting works"""
    import subprocess
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["poetry", "run", "ruff", "check", "backend/app/main.py"],
        capture_output=True
    )
    # Should not error out
    assert result.returncode in [0, 1]
```

### 3. Implementation checklist

- [ ] **Initialize Poetry**
  - [ ] backend/pyproject.toml - Create with poetry init
  - [ ] Migrate all requirements.txt dependencies to [tool.poetry.dependencies]
  - [ ] Add dev dependencies: pytest, pytest-asyncio, ruff, mypy, testcontainers, coverage
  - [ ] Run: poetry install
  - [ ] Verify: poetry run python -c "import fastapi; print('success')"

- [ ] **Configure Ruff**
  - [ ] backend/pyproject.toml:tool.ruff - Add configuration (line-length=100, target-version="py311")
  - [ ] backend/pyproject.toml:tool.ruff.lint - Add select rules (E, W, F, I, B, C4, UP)
  - [ ] backend/pyproject.toml:tool.ruff.format - Add format config (quote-style="double")
  - [ ] Run: poetry run ruff check backend/app/
  - [ ] Document known issues in issue tracker (don't fix all at once)

- [ ] **Setup Testcontainers**
  - [ ] tests/conftest.py - Create new file with testcontainer fixtures
  - [ ] tests/conftest.py:postgres_container() - PostgreSQL container fixture
  - [ ] tests/conftest.py:redis_container() - Redis container fixture
  - [ ] tests/conftest.py:test_engine() - Async SQLAlchemy engine with testcontainer
  - [ ] tests/conftest.py:db_session() - Clean database session per test
  - [ ] Update existing tests to use new fixtures (start with 1-2 tests as proof of concept)

- [ ] **Update CI Pipeline**
  - [ ] .gitlab-ci.yml:test - Add test stage with poetry run pytest
  - [ ] .gitlab-ci.yml:lint - Add lint stage with poetry run ruff check
  - [ ] .gitlab-ci.yml:format-check - Add format check stage with poetry run ruff format --check
  - [ ] Configure stages to run on every push/PR
  - [ ] Make test failures blocking (exit code !=0 fails pipeline)

- [ ] **Documentation**
  - [ ] README.md - Update setup instructions to use Poetry
  - [ ] README.md - Add Ruff usage instructions (poetry run ruff check/format)
  - [ ] README.md - Add testing instructions with testcontainers
  - [ ] backend/pyproject.toml - Add project metadata (name, description, version)

- [ ] **Verification**
  - [ ] Run: poetry install (succeeds, no errors)
  - [ ] Run: poetry run pytest tests/test_tooling.py (all new tests pass)
  - [ ] Run: poetry run ruff check backend/app/ (runs without crashing, documents issues)
  - [ ] Run: poetry run ruff format --check backend/app/ (runs without crashing)
  - [ ] Verify CI pipeline runs tests automatically on new commit
  - [ ] Verify Docker containers work with poetry (update Dockerfile if needed)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Poetry manages all dependencies (pyproject.toml + poetry.lock committed)
- [ ] poetry install works without errors
- [ ] poetry run pytest works with testcontainers
- [ ] Testcontainers successfully start PostgreSQL and Redis in tests
- [ ] Ruff checks can run (poetry run ruff check .)
- [ ] Ruff format check can run (poetry run ruff format --check .)
- [ ] CI pipeline runs tests on every push/PR
- [ ] CI pipeline reports test failures as build failures
- [ ] README.md updated with Poetry setup instructions
- [ ] At least 1-2 existing tests migrated to use testcontainers (proof of concept)
- [ ] Docker build still works with Poetry (backend Dockerfile updated if needed)
- [ ] Pre-commit hooks NOT YET installed (deferred to Phase 2)
- [ ] Tests passing (both new tooling tests and existing tests)
design:
## Goal

Establish modern Python development toolchain and testing infrastructure as the foundation for production-readiness improvements. This task delivers Poetry for dependency management, Ruff for linting/formatting, and Testcontainers for realistic integration testing.

## Effort Estimate

8-10 hours total:
- Poetry setup: 2-3 hours (migration, troubleshooting)
- Ruff configuration: 1 hour (config, document issues)
- Testcontainers: 3-4 hours (fixtures, migrate 2 tests, CI Docker-in-Docker)
- CI pipeline: 1-2 hours (configuration, testing)
- Documentation: 1 hour (README updates)

## Implementation

### 1. Study existing code patterns

**Current dependency management:**
- backend/requirements.txt:18 - Current pip-based dependencies (fastapi>=0.109.0, sqlalchemy>=2.0.25, etc.)
- No pyproject.toml exists yet

**Current testing setup:**
- tests/ directory with 15 test files
- tests/test_api.py:1195 - Main integration test suite
- No pytest.ini or conftest.py for centralized configuration
- Uses SQLite in-memory for tests (need to replace with PostgreSQL testcontainers)

**Current linting:**

- No pre-commit hooks installed
- .gitlab-ci.yml doesn't run linting or tests

**Current Docker setup:**
- Dockerfile exists for backend service
- Uses pip install -r requirements.txt
- Will need update to use Poetry

### 2. Write tests first (TDD)

**Tests to create:**

```python
# tests/test_tooling.py - Verify new tooling works

import pytest
from testcontainers.postgres import PostgresContainer
from testcontainers.redis import RedisContainer


def test_poetry_dependencies_installed():
    """Verify Poetry installed all required dependencies with correct versions"""
    import fastapi
    import sqlalchemy
    from sqlalchemy import __version__ as sa_version
    
    # Verify SQLAlchemy 2.0+ (requirement for async)
    major_version = int(sa_version.split('.')[0])
    assert major_version >= 2, f"SQLAlchemy {sa_version} < 2.0"
    
    # Verify core dependencies importable
    import pytest
    import pydantic
    import celery
    
    # Note: ruff is command-line tool, not importable Python package


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_postgres_testcontainer():
    """Verify PostgreSQL testcontainer starts and accepts connections"""
    with PostgresContainer("postgres:15-alpine") as postgres:
        conn_url = postgres.get_connection_url()
        assert "postgresql" in conn_url
        assert postgres.get_container_host_ip()
        
        # Verify actual connection works
        from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text
        engine = create_engine(conn_url)
        with engine.connect() as conn:
            result = conn.execute(text("SELECT 1"))
            assert result.scalar() == 1


def test_redis_testcontainer():
    """Verify Redis testcontainer starts and accepts connections"""
    with RedisContainer("redis:7-alpine") as redis:
        assert redis.get_container_host_ip()
        port = redis.get_exposed_port(6379)
        assert port
        
        # Verify actual connection works
        import redis as redis_client
        client = redis_client.Redis(
            host=redis.get_container_host_ip(),
            port=int(port)
        )
        assert client.ping() == True


def test_ruff_format_check_passes_on_formatted_file():
    """Verify Ruff format check works and returns correct exit codes"""
    import subprocess
    
    # Create known-formatted Python file
    import tempfile
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='w', suffix='.py', delete=False) as f:
        f.write('"""Test module."""\n\ndef hello() -> str:\n    return "world"\n')
        temp_file = f.name
    
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["poetry", "run", "ruff", "format", "--check", temp_file],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True
        )
        # Should pass on properly formatted file
```

## Key Considerations (ADDED BY SRE REVIEW)

### Edge Case: Poetry Version Conflicts

**Problem:** requirements.txt may have conflicting version constraints that pip ignores but Poetry catches.

**Example:**
```
fastapi>=0.109.0
pydantic>=2.0.0
some-package==1.0.0  # depends on pydantic<2.0
```

**Mitigation:**
- Run `poetry add` for each dependency individually
- If conflict occurs, Poetry will report it immediately
- Manually resolve by choosing compatible versions or removing conflicting package
- Document resolution in commit message for future reference

**Rollback:** If Poetry migration fails with unresolvable conflicts, keep requirements.txt temporarily and create bd task to resolve conflicts before re-attempting.

### Edge Case: Testcontainers Docker Requirements

**Problem:** Testcontainers requires Docker daemon accessible without sudo, which may not be configured.

**Detection:**
```bash
docker ps  # Should succeed without sudo
```

**If fails:**
1. Add user to docker group: `sudo usermod -aG docker $USER`
2. Log out and back in
3. Verify: `docker ps` works without sudo

**CI Environment:**
- GitLab CI requires Docker-in-Docker service (docker:dind)
- DOCKER_HOST must be set to tcp://docker:2375
- If CI tests fail with "Cannot connect to Docker daemon", Docker-in-Docker is missing

**Rollback:** If Docker configuration impossible, defer testcontainers to Phase 2 and continue using SQLite for Phase 1.

### Edge Case: Ruff Format Destructive Changes

**Problem:** `ruff format` (without --check) modifies files in-place and cannot be undone except via git.

**Prevention:**
- ALWAYS run `ruff format --check` first to preview changes
- Review diff before applying: `ruff format --diff`
- Only run `ruff format` (destructive) after review
- Commit before running destructive format (enables git reset)

**If accidental format:**
```bash
git diff  # Review changes
git checkout -- .  # Undo if undesired
```

### Edge Case: CI Docker Image Pull Rate Limits

**Problem:** DockerHub rate limits unauthenticated pulls (100/6h per IP). CI may hit limit pulling postgres:15-alpine, redis:7-alpine.

**Detection:** CI fails with "toomanyrequests: You have reached your pull rate limit"

**Mitigation:**
1. Use GitLab Container Registry mirrors (if available)
2. Authenticate DockerHub in CI (add DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG variable)
3. Cache images in CI (GitLab caching)

**Temporary workaround:** Use smaller test scope until rate limit resets.

### Edge Case: Poetry Lock File Platform Differences

**Problem:** poetry.lock includes platform-specific hashes. Lock file generated on Linux may fail validation on macOS, or vice versa.

**Symptoms:** `poetry install` fails with "Hash mismatch" error.

**Mitigation:**
- Generate poetry.lock on Linux (matches production environment)
- If developing on macOS, add `--no-cache` flag: `poetry install --no-cache`
- Alternatively, regenerate lock file: `poetry lock --no-update`

**CI:** Always use Linux-based CI image (python:3.11-slim) to match production.

### Edge Case: Testcontainer Cleanup Failures

**Problem:** If test crashes or is interrupted (Ctrl+C), testcontainer may not clean up, leaving orphaned Docker containers.

**Detection:**
```bash
docker ps -a | grep testcontainers
```

**Cleanup:**
```bash
docker ps -a | grep testcontainers | awk '{print $1}' | xargs docker rm -f
docker volume prune -f
```

**Prevention:** Use pytest fixtures with proper cleanup (yield pattern in conftest.py handles cleanup automatically).

### Performance Consideration: Testcontainer Startup Time

**Problem:** Starting PostgreSQL and Redis containers adds 10-20 seconds to first test run.

**Mitigation:**
- Use session-scoped fixtures (containers shared across all tests in session)
- Containers start once per `pytest` invocation, not per test
- Subsequent test runs fast (cached images)
- CI: Cache Docker images between pipeline runs (GitLab caching)

**Expected Test Times:**
- First run (pulling images): 30-60 seconds for setup + test execution
- Subsequent runs (cached images): 10-15 seconds for setup + test execution
- Pure test execution (after setup): <5 seconds for 20 tests

### Reference Implementations

**Similar Poetry migration:** Review how other FastAPI projects migrated:
- FastAPI documentation: uses Poetry
- FastAPI template repos: poetry init patterns

**Testcontainers patterns:** Review existing projects using testcontainers-python:
- Official examples: https://github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-python
- PostgreSQL fixtures: https://testcontainers-python.readthedocs.io/en/latest/postgres/

**Ruff configuration:** Review Ruff documentation:
- Configuration options: https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/configuration/
- Rules reference: https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/

## Anti-Patterns (ADDED BY SRE REVIEW)

- ❌ NO committing pyproject.toml without poetry.lock (reason: lock file ensures reproducible installs, missing lock = version drift)
- ❌ NO adding poetry.lock to .gitignore (reason: lock file MUST be in version control, otherwise CI/production get different versions)
- ❌ NO installing testcontainers in production dependencies (reason: dev-only, adds unnecessary Docker client to production, use --group dev)
- ❌ NO running `ruff format` without `--check` first (reason: destructive, modifies files in-place, review changes before applying)
- ❌ NO modifying .gitlab-ci.yml without testing locally with gitlab-runner (reason: CI syntax errors block entire pipeline, test first)
- ❌ NO breaking existing Docker build without verifying fix (reason: production deployment depends on Docker, must verify before commit)
- ❌ NO skipping poetry.lock commit (reason: CI and production need exact same dependency versions, lock file provides this)
- ❌ NO using `poetry add` without version constraints for new dependencies (reason: uncontrolled upgrades break builds, always specify "^X.Y" or ">=X.Y,<Z")
- ❌ NO running tests without Docker daemon running (reason: testcontainers fail immediately, wasting time, check Docker first: docker ps)
- ❌ NO ignoring Ruff issues in Phase 1 without documenting them (reason: technical debt tracking required, create bd tasks for each issue category)
